differences_from_lex: JOBS_TOKENS/JOBS_PORT/JOBS_DB/JOBS_HOST environment variables -> flag --tokens (and the skeleton's --port); no DB flag, no host flag

SQLite + lex-orm -> in-memory fixed-capacity boxed slices in App; nothing persists across restarts (brief says so); the 'database is never touched' wording becomes 'nothing else is looked at or changed'
SQL-injection requirements (3) become 'invalid state/limit/after values are 400'; the checks are kept with the same hostile values
loopback-only listening (req 8) dropped: a cancho listener binds all interfaces; attack's listens_on_loopback_only check removed
grants net,sql,env,fs_write -> allowed effects args,heap,clock,net_in,conn_accept,conn_read,conn_write,poll,io_write,err_write, checked via SVC_AUTHORITY_OK / cancho authority
no lex-web/lex-schema: std.http, std.json, std.route, server.reply are the toolbox; 16 KiB request buffer and 64 KiB output buffer are properties of the skeleton
401 is now returned for ALL paths before routing (the Lex brief was silent on unknown paths); header must be exactly 'Bearer <token>'

the brief states payload length in Unicode characters and the list page budget (48000 bytes, may return fewer than limit) which Lex did not need; next_after is defined as the last id in jobs, null when empty
added: 405 or 404 for wrong methods, 503 when the fixed store is full (>= 2000 jobs and 2 MiB of text must fit, reference holds 5000 jobs / 6 MiB)
pitfalls: app_handle gets App by &! borrow; 'app.jobs = vec.push(heap, app.jobs, x)' is refused (expected Vec, found &!a Vec): a growable Vec/Buffer/Map field cannot be moved out of and replaced, so state must be fixed-capacity box_slice stores written through contents(app.field); the brief tells the builder

std.http trims trailing whitespace of header values, so 'Bearer tokA ' reaches the app as 'Bearer tokA' and cannot be refused; the Lex attack's 'trailing space must not crash (200 or 401)' became 'a longer / shorter token is 401'

a response is first offered to the socket and only the unsent remainder must fit the 64 KiB per-connection queue, so on loopback a 100 KB answer usually arrives intact; the page-budget requirement is therefore checked by the answer's size (<64 KiB, observed with a late reader) and by a late-reader read; a slow-reader cut-off needs a kernel that absorbs little, so the 'whole page' check alone is not reliable on macOS
Python json.dumps escapes non-ASCII to \uXXXX (6 bytes a character), which pushes a 1000-character payload of 'e-acute' over the 4096-byte body limit; the multi-byte test sends raw UTF-8
std.json.string_into/string_length decode escapes; kind and payload must be checked after decoding (kind '\u0061bc' is the valid kind 'abc'), payload length is utf8.count of the decoded bytes
json.tape_len(body) ints is up to 98 KB for a 4096-byte body: use box_slice on the heap, not a region (an arena is one 64 KiB chunk and exhaustion traps)

'copy_into' is a builtin name and may not be redefined; a byte is not an int (int_of); no break/continue; Option/Result are enums, not helper functions; fn rows are exact ([heap] only if the body allocates)
the equivalent mutant 'acc = 0' in ct_equal (zero-padding already differs) is not detectable: constant-time cannot be observed, only the no-prefix-match behaviour
tested on macOS (cranelift) only; Linux behaviour of the late-reader check is untested here
dropped_checks: listens on loopback only by default (Lex attack check 11)
'server starts with grants net,sql,env,fs_write' -> replaced by the authority check and a plain start check
'trailing space must not crash (200 or 401)' -> impossible to observe (see pitfalls); replaced by longer/shorter/prefixed token checks
'lowercase scheme must not crash (200 or 401)' -> now exactly 401 because the brief fixes 'Bearer ' exactly

403 for a foreign claim/complete: foreign claim and missing claim give the identical response
unknown fields accepted: unknown field holding a long array -> 400
no list page budget: ... and that page is under 64 KiB
payload length in bytes: payload of 1000 two-byte characters -> 201 (characters, not bytes)
list ignores tenant: tenant list shows only own jobs
